For the Petitioners : Mr. Ajit Kumar, Sr. Advocate  Mr. Chanchal Jain, Advocate For the State : Mr. Saket Kumar, A.P.P.

For the O.P. No.2 : Mr. Rishav Kumar, Advocate 9/Dated: 16/02/2024 Heard Mr. Ajit Kumar, learned senior counsel for the petitioners, Mr. Saket Kumar, learned counsel for the State and Mr. Rishav Kumar, learned counsel for the O.P. No.2 2.

This petition has been filed for quashing the entire criminal proceeding in connection with Sadar P.S. Case No. 134/2018, corresponding to G.R. No. 660 of 2018, pending in the Court of learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Hazaribagh.

3. The complaint case has been filed alleging therein that in October, 2016 petitioners along with co-accused Rajesh Kumar Jain approached O.P. No.2 for grant of friendly loan of Rs. 50,00,000/-
and after much persuasion the O.P. no. 2 gave a loan of Rs. 60,00,000/- to the Petitioner no. 1 whereas Petitioner no. 2 & 3 along with aforesaid co- accused agreed to repay the entire loan within 3 months.

When the loan amount was not returned within 3 months the O.P. no. 2 approached the accused persons for repayment of loan after which an agreement was executed between the O.P. no.
2 and co-accused Rajesh Kumar Jain whereby it was agreed that the entire amount is paid within 8-10 months in 5 installments.
On the date of agreement the balance payable to the O.P. no. 2 was Rs. 50,97,250/-.

Thereafter only assurance was given by the accused persons to the O.P. no. 2 Raj Kumar Jain vs The State Of Jharkhand & Anr. ...... Opp. ... on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18990152/

sentences.text: regarding repayment of loan however, no amount was paid to him.

In October 2017 when the O.P.
no. 2 came to the shop of the Petitioners he was told by the Petitioners that his agreement is with co-accused Rajesh Kumar Jain and that the sum shall be paid by the said co-accused only.

The O.P.
no. 2 then issued legal notice upon the accused persons and when no reply was received he again visited the shop of the Petitioners after which the Petitioners got furious and assaulted the O.P. no.
2.
They also threatened the O.P. no. 2 that if he is ever seen they shall finish him as well as his family.

4. I.A. No. 8103 of 2019 has been filed for amendment in the prayer portion and prayer has been made for quashing of order dated 20.08.2019 whereby the learned court has been pleased to issue process under section 82 of Cr.P.C.
5.

I.A. No. 7069 of 2019 has been filed for amendment in prayer portion and prayer has been made for quashing the order dated 10.07.2019 whereby warrant of arrest has been issued against the petitioners.
6. Learned senior counsel for the petitioners submits process under section 82 of Cr.P.C. has been issued without following the parameters of that section.

7. The said submissions is being opposed by Mr. Rishav Kumar, learned counsel for the O.P. No.2 on the ground that the petitioners have not appeared before the learned court that is learned court has rightly passed the said order.
8. Considering that earlier the interim protection was provided to the petitioners and the matter is still pending to avoid multiplicity the prayer made in the I.A. is allowed.
9. I.A. No. 8103 of 2019 is allowed and disposed of.

10. Let I.A. No. 8103 of 2019 be treated as part of the main petition.
11.

Mr. Ajit Kumar, learned senior counsel for the petitioners submits that the learned court has sent the complaint under section 156(3) of Cr.P.C. pursuant to that Sadar P.S. Case No. 134 of 2018 has been registered.
He further submits that in the F.I.R. there is not allegation so far these petitioners are concerned.

By way of referring content of the F.I.R. he submits that allegations are made against Rajesh Kumar Jain that he has taken Rs. 50,97,250/- however, he has issued a cheque of Rs.
10,00,000/- in favour of O.P. No.2 for that the O.P. No. 2 has already filed case under section 138 of N.I. Act which is numbered as Complaint Case No. 1346 of 2018 which is still pending.

By way of referring legal notice he submits that in legal notice also there is no allegation so far these petitioners are concerned and the petitioner no.1 is the father of Rajesh Kumar Jain and petitioner nos. 2 and 3 are brothers of Rajesh Kumar Jain.
He submits that maliciously the present case has been filed against the petitioners and the accused Rajesh Kumar Jain is not petitioner in this petition.
On this background he submits that there is no entrustment to these petitioners.
Further there is no allegation of any intention of cheating right from very beginning so far these petitioners are concerned.

He relied in the case of "Satischandra Ratanlal Shah Vs. State of Gujarat and Raj Kumar Jain vs The State Of Jharkhand & Anr. ...... Opp. ... on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18990152/
2 Another"(2019) 9 SCC 148.

entities.text: Satischandra Ratanlal Shah Vs. State of Gujarat and Raj Kumar Jain vs The State Of Jharkhand & Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
He refers to paras 11, 12, 13 and 14 of the said judgment which is quoted hereinbelow:-
"11.
Having observed the background principles applicable herein, we need a to consider the individual charges against the appellant.
Turning to Section 405 read with Section 406 IPC, we observe that the dispute arises out of a loan transaction between the parties.
It falls from the record that Respondent 2 knew the appellant and the attendant circumstances before lending the loan,
Further it is an admitted fact that in order to recover the aforesaid amount, Respondent 2 had instituted a summary civil suit which is still pending adjudication.
The law clearly recognises a difference between simple payment/investment of money and entrustment of money or property.

A mere breach of a promise, agreement or contract does not, ipso facto,
constitute the offence of the criminal breach of trust contained in Section 405 IPC without there being a clear case of entrustment.

12. In this context, we may note that there is nothing either in the complaint or in any material before us, pointing to the fact that any property was entrusted to the appellant at all which he dishonestly converted for his own use so as to satisfy the ingredients of Section 405 punishable under Section 406 IPC.
Hence the learned Magistrate committed a serious error in issuing process against the appellant for the said offence.
Unfortunately, the High Court also failed to d correct this manifest error.
13. Now coming to the charge under Section 415 punishable under Section 420 IPC.
In the context of contracts, the distinction between mere breach of contract and cheating would depend upon the fraudulent inducement and mens rea.
(See Hridaya Ranjan Prasad Verma v. State of Bihar,)

entities.text: Hridaya Ranjan Prasad Verma v. State of Bihar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the case before us, admittedly the appellant was trapped in economic crisis and therefore, he had approached Respondent 2 to ameliorate the situation of crisis.
Further, in order to recover the aforesaid amount, Respondent 2 had instituted a summary civil suit seeking recovery of the loan amount which is still pending adjudication.

The mere inability of the appellant to return the loan amount cannot give rise to a criminal prosecution for cheating unless fraudulent or dishonest intention is shown right at the beginning of the transaction, as it is this mens rea which is the crux of the offence.
Even if all the facts in the complaint and material are taken on their face value, no such dishonest representation or inducement could be found or inferred.
14. Moreover, this Court in a number of cases has usually cautioned against criminalising civil disputes, such as breach of contractual obligations (refer to Gian Singh v. State of Punjab).

entities.text: Gian Singh v. State of Punjab
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The legislature intended to criminalise only those breaches which are accompanied by fraudulent, dishonest or deceptive inducements,
which resulted in involuntary and inefficient transfers, under Section 415 I.P.C.
Raj Kumar Jain vs The State Of Jharkhand & Anr. ...... Opp. ... on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18990152/
3 12.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Relying on the above judgment he submits that if any case is there that is for recovery of amount for that complaint case has already been filed by the O.P. No.2 under section 138 of N.I. Act.
On these backgrounds he submits that the entire criminal proceeding may be quashed.

13. Mr. Rishav Kumar, learned counsel for the O.P. No.2 vehemently opposes the prayer of quashing on the ground that this Court may not interfere at this stage as there is subsequent development in the case and chargesheet has been submitted.
He submits that there are allegation against the petitioners of hurling abuse.
He submits that there are parameters of quashing the proceeding under section 482 of Cr.P.C. and the allegations of the complaint are required to be scrutinized with great care and circumspection.
On these grounds, he submits that this petition may be dismissed.
14. Learned counsel for the State submits that the learned court has rightly passed the impugned orders.
15. Looking into complaint petition so far these petitioners are concerned, there are no allegation against the petitioners.

Allegations are made against Rajesh Kumar Jain that he has taken Rs.
50,97,250/- however, he has issued a cheque of Rs. 10,00,000/- in favour of O.P. No.2 for that the O.P. No. 2 has already filed case under section 138 of N.I. Act which is numbered as Complaint Case No. 1346 of 2018 which is still pending.
The petitioner nos. 1 is father of Rajesh Kumar Jain and petitioner nos. 2 and 3 are brothers of Rajesh Kumar Jain.
Legal notice was issued addressed to Rajesh Kumar Jain who is not petitioner in this petition.
The allegations are made only against Rajesh Kumar Jain.
Thus, looking into the contents of F.I.R. entrustment or intention of cheating from the very beginning is not made out.
Only bald allegation is made out that these petitioners have abused the complainant which suggests that only to implicate the petitioners the said averment is made in the complaint petition.

In this background if such allegations are there the High Court is having responsibility to read the things in between the lines as the case is maliciously filed every care is being taken to draft the contents of F.I.R. in such way that ingredients may be put.
16.

The argument of learned counsel for the O.P. No.2 is not being accepted by this Court with regard to further development in the matter considering that it is well settled that at any stage the High Court can exercise power under section 482 of Cr.P.C. if court comes to the conclusion that maliciously the case has been registered.

Reference may be made to the case of "Anand Kumar Mohatta and Another Vs. State (NCT of Delhi), Department of Home and Another"(2019) 11 SCC 706.
17.

No. 660 of 2018, pending in the Court of learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Hazaribagh, so far these petitioners are concerned, is quashed.

The learned court shall proceed in accordance with law.
